gamespot.com/articles/tango-into-the-dan.excerpt: Since Phantom Blade Zero ’s reveal back in… 2023?! Really? Wow, it’s been that long. Since its reveal, the action RPG has been stuck in my brain like a dream I can’t quite escape. Its fast-paced combat, which delicately combines offense and defense, looks like a dance of death, as gripping as it is dangerous. I’m ready to dive into the Phantom World, and if you are, too, you may as well save some money with a pre-order discount. My excitement has only grown with the recent wave of previews ahead of the game’s release. The promise of intense, satisfying action in GameSpot’s Phantom Blade Zero preview from Max Blumenthal only made me more excited for the upcoming game. While I have yet to see whether it can join my list of the best RPGs , there’s a good chance it might. You play as Soul, an assassin and all-around badass-looking member of The Order. Despite his hard work, he finds himself framed for murder, hunted by his former colleagues, and eventually left with a fatal wound to his heart. Fortunately, that’s not the end of Soul’s story. He’s revived, albeit with a tainted heart, and it’s up to you to uncover why he’s been dragged into a conspiracy surrounding the death of The Order’s patriarch. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mOncuUWLipQ Of course, this isn’t a murder mystery game—it’s an action game. That means Soul isn’t solving the case through clues, but through the rhythm of battle. Armed with two swords as his primary weapons and a diverse selection of secondary weapons known as Phantom Edges, including cannons and lances, you’ll battle all manner of foes. What makes Phantom Blade Zero so intriguing, and its combat look so energetic and unique, is that every battle feels like a dance. You’re not simply attacking or defending; each move seems to blend the two. It makes every fight look fluid, engaging, and satisfying. gamespot.com/articles/ubisofts-latest-re.title: Ubisoft’s Latest Restructuring Plan Puts Trials Developer RedLynx On The Chopping Block
gamespot.com/articles/ubisofts-latest-re.excerpt: Ubisoft has announced that it plans to shut down Trials developer RedLynx as part of its ongoing restructuring efforts, as well as reduce the workforce of its Skull and Bones studio, Ubisoft Singapore, by laying off 72 people. The closure of the Finland-based RedLynx is in a proposal stage, and Ubisoft says that because the studio isn't currently working on a new project, it makes more economic sense to close it down and retrench its 52 employees instead. Under Finnish law (via Kotaku ), Ubisoft is legally required to consult and negotiate with employees before it makes major changes to the studio, which is why Ubisoft hasn't officially announced yet that it will shut down RedLynx--although it's likely only a matter of time. The studio was first formed in 2000, and it's best known for its series of challenging--but highly enjoyable--Trials games, 2.5D motorcycle platforming games that require players to master their vehicle, gravity, and overcome a series of increasingly dangerous obstacle courses. Ubisoft acquired the studio in 2011, and RedLynx's Trials HD quickly became a breakout hit on the Xbox Arcade marketplace. Several games in the Trails franchise have been released over the years, with the last one being Trials Rising in 2019. Since then, RedLynx assisted Massive Entertainment with the Google Stadia port of The Division 2 and the Switch 2 port of Star Wars Outlaws, and it also produced the 2023 mobile game Gwen's Getaway. Last year, RedLynx lost 60 staff members during a restructuring wave at Ubisoft and it was announced that it would pivot to making mobile games. Trials Rising Meanwhile, Ubisoft Singapore is projected to be losing as much as 20% of its workforce. Established in 2008, it assisted on development of several Assassin's Creed games and it was the lead developer on Skull and Bones, Ubisoft's naval warfare game set in the golden age of piracy. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-leaks-are-st.excerpt: Rockstar Games has reacted to the mass GTA 6 leaks, which began in 2022, with a top developer at the studio saying it "feels like somebody's wading through your dirty washing." Bloomberg published these comments from Rockstar developers on the same day that GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek posted yet another gameplay leak, saying it could be the last. "It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” Rockstar North's Aaron Garbut said. “It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that. It’s really weirdly invasive. And so it’s quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.” https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XpPpqZwUwl0 Rockstar and Take-Two eventually tracked down the hacker who was allegedly responsible for the leaks in 2022. This person will reportedly face court on November 9 , just days before GTA 6 releases. The hack pushed Rockstar to implement a controversial new policy requiring developers to work from the office, as opposed to remotely. Rockstar publishing boss Jennifer Kolbe said Rockstar will take another look at this policy after GTA 6 is released, but she doesn't envision major changes. "The idea that we would have the game in that many environments is something that I think the security team would not love,” she said. “I think if we did not have a game that people wanted to steal as much, maybe it would be an easier conversation.” The major 2022 hack that led to a series of GTA 6 leaks was followed up by a new round of leaks this year from someone going by CyberLeek. The person, or group, was pushing a memecoin , but is apparently now shutting down . One final gameplay leak was published today, October 14, and it's a big one, so be aware of that when you're scrolling through your feed. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-could-have-b.title: GTA 6 Could Have Been Even Bigger And Released Years Sooner, But Then These Things Happened
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-could-have-b.excerpt: A big new report revealed more details about Rockstar's long-awaited GTA 6 , including how the game's scope was originally much bigger and that the game could have released years sooner. Bloomberg reported that when a small team from Rockstar traveled to Miami in 2015 to begin planning GTA 6, they envisioned the game spanning "big swaths of land across both North and South America." It was in development under the codename Project Americas at this time. The report went on to say that Rockstar would pare down GTA 6's scope to include Miami and its surrounding areas instead of the original ambition. It's not a small world, though, as GTA 6's map is 3X bigger than the map in Rockstar's last game, 2018's Red Dead Redemption II. In addition to GTA 6's version of Miami with Vice City, the game takes players to a range of other locations in greater Leonida, which is a stand-in for Florida. The confirmed major locations in GTA 6 so far include: Vice City Leonida Keys Grassrivers Port Gellhorn Ambrosia Mount Kalaga Port Gellhorn in GTA 6. The report also digs into how Rockstar originally planned to develop GTA 6 concurrently with Red Dead Redemption II, which would have helped GTA 6 come to market sooner. However, as the scope for Red Dead Redemption II grew, Rockstar's Rob Nelson came to realize he needed to assign more staff at Rockstar's network of studios to help get the Western out the door in 2018. According to Bloomberg, this meant GTA 6 would be delayed "several years," but one silver lining was how the work that went into Red Dead Redemption II would "pay off when we get to the game [GTA 6]." Nelson pointed out that Rockstar, at one point in time, developed multiple games concurrently across offices, but now, Rockstar's network of teams work on one project together before moving on to the next. gamespot.com/articles/hyrule-field-sure-.title: Hyrule Field Sure Feels Empty In Ocarina Of Time These Days
gamespot.com/articles/hyrule-field-sure-.excerpt: The young adventurer Link has been entrusted with an epic quest that will take him to every corner of the globe. He is fated to do incredible things, to become the Hero of Time, but for now he is just a boy. He says farewell to his dearest friend, Saria, and, with his trusty sword and his fairy Navi in tow, he steps out of his tiny community of forest children and finds himself in awe of the wider world. As he gazes out, he realizes this vast untamed wilderness is … maybe the size of a couple of football fields? Thereabouts? I was there when Ocarina of Time first released in 1998, and like many young gamers, my mind was blown. This was one of our earliest experiences with 3D exploration in an open world, and it truly felt vast. The central hub of Hyrule Field was large enough to gracefully cross on horseback. Almost 30 years later, though, the once-majestic Hyrule Field lacks its original luster. I recently got to play the Ocarina of Time remake , and like lots of players, I was curious how--or if--Hyrule Field would be updated for this latest incarnation of the game. The answer is that it's very faithful to the original, for better and worse. The size appears roughly the same, and the landscape is mostly empty aside from the spokes leading out from the hub and Lon Lon Ranch at its center. There appear to be a few more irregular hills and rock formations to add realistic texture, but it is largely recognizable. On one hand, this makes sense. As I mentioned in my preview, this remake aims to respectfully recreate the original Ocarina of Time, and complicating Hyrule Field with a bunch of random stuff wouldn't feel authentic. Your default run speed is a little faster, so it doesn't feel like it's wasting your time crossing an empty field. It mostly exists as a space between the towns and dungeons you visit for quests. gamespot.com/articles/zelda-ocarina-of-t.title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake’s Dedicated Jump Button Is Good, Actually
gamespot.com/articles/zelda-ocarina-of-t.excerpt: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake looks to be a mostly faithful modernization of the classic game, with a few quality-of-life tweaks and updated visuals to make it play like a modern game. One of the more controversial of these is the addition of a jump button, which the original game famously lacked. But now having gotten hands-on with the remake , I can say that the addition of a jump is a good change, and Ocarina is better for it. Ocarina was designed without a jump button, and to be clear, the addition of one doesn't transform this into a platformer. Based on my limited experience, the need to jump is occasional and often simple, just clearing small gaps. This geometry was never created to ask you to handle complex jumping challenges and the remake doesn't appear to have any intention of changing that. My demo covered the beginning of the game in Kokiri Forest and into the Deku Tree, first exploring Hyrule Field and Hyrule Castle Town, and some of the Forest Temple with adult Link. The jump button made it feel more natural to hop across streams in Kokiri Forest, and to clear the small boulder challenge to obtain Link's first sword. In Hyrule Field, I was able to freely jump on top of a rock and then control how I jumped off. And in the Great Deku Tree and Forest Temple, I found that jumping fit naturally into the exploration, as I would easily hop onto a wall of vines to start my ascent. Most importantly, the jump button just felt like it should be there, because modern games feel lacking without one. I tried to imagine the same encounters in the classic Ocarina style, in which you'd just walk up to a ledge and automatically jump, and it just wouldn't be the same. This version of OOT looks modern, and so it only seems right that it should play modern too. It may seem like heresy to add a jump button to Ocarina of Time, but after only a few minutes of play, it felt completely instinctive. gamespot.com/articles/epic-is-overhaulin.title: Epic Is Overhauling Its Anti-Cheat So That Fortnite Can Finally Come To A New Platform
gamespot.com/articles/epic-is-overhaulin.excerpt: Thanks to devices such as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, as well as the ongoing issues with Windows, gaming on Linux looks a lot more attractive over the last few years. Its biggest hurdle is still multiplayer games and their anti-cheat systems, but Epic Games is committed to bringing one of the biggest around to the operating system soon. Epic Games has announced that it is working on a Linux version for Fortnite. It's going to act as a test for Epic's overhaul of EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat) , its solution to those developing multiplayer games in Unreal Engine to prevent cheating (most recently used in Gears of War: E-Day). Epic says that it has offered Linux support for its current version of EAC, but that most developers (itself included) opted not to use it and instead omit Linux support entirely because of its inability to be as protective as its Windows version. A native rebuild of EAC, that doesn't require translation layers such as Proton, would help Epic bring the software up to par with Windows, at which point it would be comfortable finally releasing a native Linux version of Fortnite. In a blog post, Epic says that once it has reached this stage, it will make this available to other developers, too. "We are also planning to pilot EAC Linux v2 in Fortnite first, where we’ll test it in a live environment and refine it based on what we learn. Once we’ve validated EAC v2’s effectiveness, we’ll make it available to more game developers so they can bring their multiplayer games to Linux players too." Epic hasn't shared a timeline for when it expects Fortnite on Linux, but does say that its pilot program will be available through its new Epic Game Store launcher . Announced at the same time, Epic has decided to follow through with its commitment to AI-developed software earlier this week, with the new launcher labelled as "vibe coded" because "programming is hard". gamespot.com/articles/xbox-survey-about-.title: Xbox Survey About Exclusives Includes A Nuclear Strategy, But Wait Just A Minute
gamespot.com/articles/xbox-survey-about-.excerpt: Microsoft is reportedly surveying a subset of Xbox users about changing its plans for exclusive games going forward--possibly in a big way--and that's no surprise given Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has alluded to changes to the exclusivity strategy in the future . At the same time, a survey like this is not necessarily indicative of anything beyond Microsoft conducting research. After all, there is an entire team at Xbox called Xbox Research that ... researches all manner of things, and the results of that research doesn't always lead to changes in the marketplace. Windows Central reports that a new survey was issued to some Xbox Insiders this week, and the site confirmed the survey to be real. The survey asks how members might feel about the totally nuclear option of making all Xbox-developed games except Call of Duty exclusive to Xbox on console. "Imagine it was announced that all future title releases from every Xbox-developed gaming franchise except Call of Duty will be console-exclusive to Xbox," the survey asks. It goes on: "For Minecraft only, existing titles would no longer be available for purchase on PlayStation or Nintendo consoles and would not receive any new content updates. However, there is no impact to any of the existing titles or content you already own. Nothing changes on PC with this announcement." The survey asks respondents to say in this scenario, where they would be most likely  to play any of the exclusive content. The choices are: On an existing Xbox I own On a new Xbox Series X|S I would decide to purchase On a PC I would skip playing because it would now be unavailable on my preferred console Something else Not interested in playing the exclusive content Another page of the survey specifically asks about Fallout, polling users about how they would feel if future Fallout games would be console-exclusive to Xbox, and with nothing changing at all on PC. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-reviews-when.title: GTA 6 Reviews: When They Could Be Released
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-reviews-when.excerpt: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 releases on November 19, but when will you be able to read reviews? According to historical precedent and a new report, reviews for the open-world crime game should be available before launch. Insider Gaming reported that reviews for GTA 6 will be posted at some point before November 19, but the exact timing is unknown for now. According to insider NateTheHate , Rockstar will send copies of GTA 6 to reviewers before the end of October, so any time now, seemingly. A scene from GTA 6. What history tells us The last GTA game, GTA 5, was released on September 17, 2013, and reviews for the game were published starting on September 16. For Rockstar's next game, 2018's Red Dead Redemption II, reviews also went live one day prior to release. This doesn't necessarily mean Rockstar will follow the same playbook for GTA 6, however. Nothing is confirmed at this stage. GTA 6 launches on November 19-- unless it's delayed again --for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's expected to be the biggest game of 2026 and maybe all time, and it's reportedly on pace to earn $2 billion in revenue before launch . A lot of new details about GTA 6 recently came to light, including how the game originally had a bigger scope and could have launched sooner , Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick’s response to a big delay , and the absurd amount of detail in the game . We also learned that GTA 6 did not in fact cost $1.5 billion to make and that an entire studio was spun up to create NPCs . Rockstar also discussed how its GTA 6 realism experiment began with beer and sandwiches and that the studio says it won’t need another eight years to release its next game. Beyond all of this, Rockstar reacted to the game's high-profile hack in 2022.

gamespot.com/articles/im-enjoying-fire-e.title: I’m Enjoying Fire Emblem More By Not Playing Fire Emblem More
gamespot.com/articles/im-enjoying-fire-e.excerpt: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave has some of the best tactical gameplay in the series to date, but actually digging into the art of seeing units bonk each other on the head in turn-based combat is a massive slog. Between a shift to Persona-like storytelling and a laundry list of chores, the game can feel like the equivalent of the Achilles and the tortoise paradox ( via a Jujutsu Kaisen breakdown ), because the closer I get to actually moving the story forward, the further I feel I am from actually engaging in some of that fantastic warfare. And that's a shame, because Fortune's Weave is a really great evolution of the core Fire Emblem gameplay experience. The tactics game has more nuance to its rock-paper-nuns-with-guns formula in this entry, the jobs system offers more variety, and the unique tools at each Flame Lord's disposal make each one a force to be reckoned with. So what's the solution to enjoying the best parts of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, without getting bogged down by all the busywork in between? It turns out that if you want to enjoy Fire Emblem more , you may need to play less of it. Don't sweat the training https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6UneVog1cME One thing I've discovered is a gameplay loop that Fire Emblem expects you to follow with each Flame Lord. Each of the main chapters is squeezed into lengthy moments of downtime, where you're free to explore to your heart's content--or within the limits of your renown and overall standing in the countryside beyond. Options include dungeon-diving, visiting gods for favors, taking training courses, mining for materials, taking on odd jobs, recruiting new members to your team, and so on. I'm busy skipping most of that as I dive into the game's later chapters. Some players have been enthusiastic about the scale of the changes, although the new economy and logistics adjustments have raised concerns among players who rely more heavily on those systems. Here are the 10 changes that will have the biggest impact on Wardogs, followed by everything new in Wardogs Season 2. Blue Team Bribery Wardogs is trying something unusual to solve a problem money alone can't usually fix: bribing players to choose the team they don't want to play. Lonestar--or the blue team--has struggled with lower win rates and earned itself quite the reputation as the cursed faction in the game. Bulkhead says that could be down to uniform visibility or spawn locations, but weird player superstitions are probably the real reason people avoid the team. Season 2 introduces extra cash and XP for Lonestar victories, plus additional rewards for certain teamplay actions. Players on any faction that's at least 40 points behind the team in second place will also receive a 20% vendor discount to encourage them to equip their best loadouts and try to recoup the loss. This is being treated as a Season 2 experiment rather than a permanent balance solution, but it remains to be seen whether the rewards are enough to change players' preference. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-helps-modern.excerpt: Rockstar's GTA 6 is releasing this November, and some believe it will blot out the sun when it comes to the impact it will have on the greater gaming market. The game could also help other titles, like Activision's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. That's according to Activision chief marketing officer Tyle Bahl, who said in an interview that GTA 6 will drive more people to gaming overall, and this could act as a rising tide that lifts all ships, including Modern Warfare 4. “Well, no offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] are the two biggest games of the year. And more people coming in to the dashboards, more people taking the dust off their Xbox or PlayStation and playing again, is going to be more eyeballs for us overall," he told The Game Business. His comment about Zelda is in reference to Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2, which launches on November 5. It's expected to be a huge hit, just like MW4 and GTA 6. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yLFRQaQT0qM Another publisher, Ubisoft, is not afraid of GTA 6, either. CEO Yves Guillemot said  when a big game like GTA 6 comes out, it helps everyone in the industry. One of Ubisoft's biggest games, Rainbow Six Siege, is actually planning to debut new content right around the time GTA 6 launches . Bahl also stated that a big differentiator for Call of Duty is "spending time with friends," and he thinks this will hold true for MW4 this year even with GTA 6 coming to market just a few weeks after MW4 releases on October 23. "When we look at our research and say, ‘What is the most exciting things about our games? Is it the gunplay?’ It’s actually spending time with friends. And so, we stand on our own [in that regard]," he said. “If more people are talking about games, if there’s more press around it, that’s going to be good for everybody, not just us.” MW4's campaign unlocks on October 16 for people who preorder, and the full game--comprising campaign, DMZ, and multiplayer--arrives for everyone o

The GTA 6 launch trailer is 90 seconds long exactly, and it gives us a closer look at some of the in-game action (and its new soundtrack composers ). While some of what see is pretty typical of games in the Grand Theft Auto series, there are a few surprising additions, and some things that hint toward just how deeply realistic the game is. Lucia starts the game in prison While an earlier trailer suggested as much, it now seems more certain that Lucia's journey in GTA 6 starts with her in prison. While working at the marina, Jason receives a call from her. While we don't know anything about the conversation that takes place after, the fact that she's still incarcerated while he's out and working tells us that he'll probably be keeping pretty close tabs on when she's getting released, especially since the two have clearly remained in contact. There's plenty of physical intimacy We already knew that Jason and Lucia would be able to get up close and personal . In the launch trailer, though, we see them spending time in bed and even in the shower together. The emphasis on intimacy alongside violent sequences adds depth to their relationship, which we already know is going to be central to the game's events. It remains to be seen the degree to which these are decisions the player takes, as opposed to being scripted into the narrative, since it's been emphasized that Jason and Lucia aren't necessarily a couple . gamespot.com/articles/street-fighter-mov.title: Street Fighter Could Be In For A Rough First Round At The Box Office
gamespot.com/articles/street-fighter-mov.excerpt: Street Fighter is officially spin-kicking its way into theaters this week, starting with previews on Thursday and leading into the crucial opening weekend. It's the second movie based on a Capcom IP to make its way to the silver screen this year--following Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film in September--but so far, early estimates for the martial arts extravaganza aren't looking too healthy. According to Deadline's box-office-predictions , Street Fighter is expected to take in under $70 million worldwide. Of that figure, it's estimated to open with a US box-office take in the high 30 millions on 3,500 screens, and a take in the mid-30 millions internationally. Typically, movies need to make at least double their production budget back to be considered successful, and with Street Fighter costing $82 million to produce, it doesn't look like it'll recoup its expenses in its first weekend. There's still a chance it could be a small hit if word of mouth drives audiences to theaters, and in terms of competition, Street Fighter has a few weeks to dominate cinemas as it'll be the biggest action film on the block--at least until the November 1 re-release of V for Vendetta, which is celebrating its 20th anniversary. The movie won't open in the potentially lucrative market of China, but internationally, the lion's share of sales is expected to come from Mexico, Brazil, the UK, Australia, and Asian markets. https://youtu.be/U6sbm1OaJb8 How does that opening stack up against other recent video game movie adaptations? Resident Evil got off to a solid start with a $60 million domestic opening last month, and so far, the film has grossed $324 million worldwide, making it a surprise commercial hit and Cregger's biggest film yet . Meanwhile, Mortal Kombat 2 did much worse when it launched in May, making only $38 million on its opening US weekend and finishing with a worldwide box office total of $129.5 million. gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-is-getting-a.title: GTA 6 Is Getting An Original Score From Electronic Duo Justice
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-is-getting-a.excerpt: With a new (and steamy) launch trailer going live to remind you of its November 19 release date, Grand Theft Auto 6 is starting to look like a slick new chapter in the series. It's also sounding like a great sequel, and that's no accident as the game features an original soundtrack by French electronic music duo Justice. On top of that, a new single from Justice called "Flower in a Hurricane" will be featured on Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album, the official game soundtrack, and the track also includes Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. If you're unfamiliar with them, Justice is a duo consisting of Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay, and they rose to fame with their 2007 album, Cross. They followed that up with Audio, Video, Disco in 2011, Woman in 2016, and after a seven-year hiatus, Hyperdrama in 2024. The pair have earned several Grammy nominations over the years and a ton of awards for their catchy mix of rock and disco themes, creating chart-topping hits. And that soundtrack will probably sound great in one of GTA 6's absurdly detailed night clubs . https://youtu.be/JWxoRY7AFSw While Justice crafts the core musical sound of GTA 6, players will also be free to flip through several radio stations and podcasts in the game. Like previous GTA entries, these encompass a wide variety of musical genres, from outlaw country rock to reggae. These will represent the “next evolution of in-game radio, and more,” Rockstar says, and players can listen to them while driving or on foot. The developer also revealed more details about the GTA 6 album, which features 34 songs written specifically for the game, including new music from Keith Richards and Travis Scott . Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch for PS5 and Xbox Series X next month, and while a PC port hasn't been announced yet, it might be coming sooner than you think. gamespot.com/articles/put-down-your-pitc.title: Put Down Your Pitchforks, GTA VI Was Always Eligible For The Game Awards This Year
gamespot.com/articles/put-down-your-pitc.excerpt: As we inch ever closer to the tidal wave that is Grand Theft Auto VI approaching over the horizon, some minds are turning to awards season and how many awards Rockstar's next epic will catch in its wake. Some, like Insider Gaming, are beginning to report that--just barely-- GTA will be eligible for The Game Awards , Geoff Keighley's annual December extravaganza, which has led others to wonder if that was by some nefarious design. The official website for The Game Awards lists November 20, 2026 at 9 PM PT as the cutoff date for this year's ceremony, which means that any game that launches before that time can be considered for nomination. As GTA VI is scheduled to launch one day earlier on November 19, that means GTA VI and TGA '26 will likely be intertwined this year. Jason and Lucia at the club. Now, before torches are lit and pitchforks are sharpened, evidence suggests that date was not put in place specifically for GTA to be eligible this year. If anything, it was Rockstar that planned around Keighley's schedule, as the Friday before Thanksgiving has routinely been the cutoff for TGA nominations. Last year, the cutoff was November 21, as referenced in this Polygon article regarding Dispatch's eligibility. In 2024, eligibility was cut off on November 22, as evidenced in this Polygon article exploring the games that missed 2024 and were eligible in 2025. 2018 was the last time a Rockstar project was eligible for The Game Awards, as Red Dead Redemption II landed 10 nominations and four wins. Notably, one of those wins was not Game Of The year, which went to Sony Santa Monica for the God of War reboot. Grand Theft Auto VI's eligibility for TGA 2026 was never in doubt--well, unless it got delayed again. Now that we're likely clear of that scenario, it's only a matter of time until we see just how many trophies are headed to Vice City.

gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-launch-trail.title: The GTA 6 Launch Trailer Shows Off Vice City And Steamy Scene With Lucia And Jason
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6-launch-trail.excerpt: Rockstar Games has published the launch trailer for GTA 6 , and it's pretty spectacular. The game has been in development for more than a decade, and it's finally set for release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The trailer features the new song, "Flower in a Hurricane" from Justice featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Justice also composed the entire original score for GTA 6. The trailer itself shows off lots more of Vice City and its people, places, and criminal activities. We also see very steamy scene with Lucia and Jason in the shower. Jason and Lucia are lovers and partners in crime, and cultivating their relationship is a big part of the game. Or, you can have them break up and just be friends who commit crimes together. The new trailer was captured on a base PS5. The trailer carries the PlayStation branding and even features an in-game controller that looks like a DualSense because Sony and Rockstar are working together to promote GTA 6. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rz1B4B2yBZY After a decade-plus of development, GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, with a PC release expected in early 2027 .

gamespot.com/articles/gta-6s-push-for-re.title: GTA 6’s Push For Realism Includes A Context-Specific Sweating System, For Real
gamespot.com/articles/gta-6s-push-for-re.excerpt: Part of the reason why Rockstar has taken so long with GTA 6 comes down to the process of crafting the fine details, and that includes a new sweat system. Reporter Jason Schreier said on his YouTube page that Rockstar created a new system in GTA 6 that will make Lucia or Jason perspire different amounts "depending on how much effort they're putting in." For example, "If they're dancing extra hard in the nightclub, they will sweat more than if they are not," he said. The sweating system is expected to also apply in other areas, like when hitting the gym or just being outside in the heat of GTA 6's version of south Florida . Lucia in a club in GTA 6. GTA 6 is not the first game to make new strides in the area of bodily fluids, as EA Sports--many years ago--made sweat look more realistic in the Madden franchise . And years before that, 2K Sports improved the in-game sweating system in the NBA 2K series . Rockstar also aimed for more realism in GTA 6 by going on ridealongs with police officers and visiting strip clubs . GTA 6 isn't a life-sim, though, and Rockstar took strides to find the balance between simulating life and making a fun experience . GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it's expected to be the biggest game ever. Despite that, its expected success will not fix the many deep and serious issues with the current video game market , experts say.

gamespot.com/articles/why-rockstar-cance.title: Why Rockstar Canceled Its PlayStation-Exclusive Follow-Up To GTA 4
gamespot.com/articles/why-rockstar-cance.excerpt: At E3 2009, Sony announced that it was partnering with Rockstar on a PlayStation-exclusive spy game called Agent , with Rockstar founders Sam and Dan Houser overseeing development. The game never materialized, though, and now Dan Houser has shared more details as to why. Speaking to IGN , Houser said Agent never coming out shouldn't be a total shock because he worked on "a bunch of games that never came out." He said Rockstar tried with two or three different teams to make Agent--an open-world spy game--but the teams just "could not get it right." "And it never came out. We concluded that it was not a game we were ever going to figure out how to make. Other people can try, but I personally think it's hard," he said. Great spy movies like the James Bond series work so well because they take viewers all over the world, but "that's not an experience in an open-world game that really works," Houser said. "So we tried lots of things and couldn't get it quite right," Houser said, going on to say that the teams built great elements but they never came together in a full package. Images of Agent, which was reportedly set in the '70s, have emerged over the years, showing off some of what Rockstar was planning. In 2009, then-Take-Two president Ben Feder told GameSpot that Agent was being positioned to be the next Grand Theft Auto . “It’s the A team working on an AAA title,” he said at the time. “I think the subject matter, the characters, the story, the environment, the background–all the elements are there. It’s such a rich environment to play in.” Across the industry, games get canceled regularly-- Blizzard has said it cancels 50% of the games it starts --but Rockstar's Agent got more traction because of the studio's profile. Rockstar never gave Agent a release date, but it would have followed up 2008's Grand Theft Auto 4. The next game that Rockstar North led development on after GTA 4 was 2013's GTA 5, and now Rockstar North is set to release GTA 6 on November 19.

gamespot.com/articles/call-of-duty-mw4-i.title: Call Of Duty: MW4 Is Not On Xbox Game Pass, But Here’s When You Can Expect It
gamespot.com/articles/call-of-duty-mw4-i.excerpt: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is set for release on October 23, and in a big shakeup, it will not be available on Xbox Game Pass at launch. This has been known for a while, but Activision is reminding people of this in a new blog post on the eve of the game's campaign early access on October 16. In fact, Activision has been warning people that MW4 is not on Game Pass for months now , so the blog post is just the latest example of this. Upon release, the only way to get MW4 is by purchasing it outright, starting at $70 for the base edition and scaling to $100 for the Vault edition. Game Pass subscribers will have to wait a year for MW4. When will MW4 come to Game Pass? Activision said MW4 will be available on Xbox Game Pass at some point at the end of next year, meaning it will be "windowed" as a standalone purchase for about one year. Why are new Call of Duty games no longer included with Game Pass? 2024’s Black Ops 6 was the first entry in the series to launch directly into Xbox Game Pass, with Black Ops 7 following the same playbook in 2025. However, Microsoft announced earlier this year that new Call of Duty titles would no longer debut in Game Pass , an announcement it made in conjunction with a price cut for the subscription service. Microsoft has never explicitly said why it made this major change, but it could have to do with lost sales. It was reported that Black Ops 6 coming to Game Pass in 2024 amounted to Microsoft missing out on hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue . That number has been debated, and it does not tell the whole story, but no doubt there was a financial impact that Microsoft is responding to. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma is undertaking a "reset" of the Xbox business, and cutting new Call of Duty games from Game Pass is part of that. She is also trying to revive Xbox console exclusives , including a nuclear option . What other Call of Duty games are on Game Pass? gamespot.com/articles/from-liberty-city-.title: From Liberty City To Leonida: Following The Evolution Of Rockstar’s GTA Launch Trailers
gamespot.com/articles/from-liberty-city-.excerpt: Rockstar has finally given us the launch trailer for GTA 6 ahead of its November 19 release date, and it looks spectacular . This shouldn’t be a surprise, considering the developer has been honing its cinematic craft for decades now as it pushes the boundaries of what games are capable of. This 90-second extravaganza is no exception, with its stellar combination of sumptuous landscapes, fascinating characters, and an impressively detailed world. But if you’ll permit me to put our mounting anticipation aside for a second, this launch trailer also represents the next step in a long journey for Rockstar. Every single blockbuster it has released over the years, whether it be San Andreas or Red Dead Redemption 2, has acted as an exceptional example of what video games can be in the modern era. To celebrate the imminent arrival of GTA 6, let’s take a look back at Rockstar launch trailers of the past and how they’ve evolved over the years. Grand Theft Auto 3 (2001) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WUi3davvBmM Nobody expected Grand Theft Auto 3 to revolutionize the medium when it first launched for PS2 back in 2001. The first two games were enjoyably chaotic romps with an incredible sense of attitude, but it wasn’t until the third core entry that Rockstar’s destiny changed forever. Even 25 years later, its release-date trailer is a confident glimpse into the pixelated grime of Liberty City. It was a living, breathing metropolis that dwarfed anything we’d seen in video games with a lead character in Claude who felt like he didn’t just exist in this world: He lived in it. There are few narrative scenes in the trailer itself, with the focus otherwise on pulling off sick handbrake turns in luscious cars or blowing away innocent pedestrians with sniper rifles. It is representative of where Rockstar--back then known as DMA Design--and its priorities sat at the time. gamespot.com/articles/007-first-light-on.title: 007 First Light On Switch 2 Includes Something No Other Platform Gets, And It’s Ridiculous
gamespot.com/articles/007-first-light-on.excerpt: IO Interactive has announced the release date for 007 First Light's long-delayed Switch 2 version--March 18, 2027--and that's not all. People who preorder the game for Switch 2 are getting something no other platform has: a ridiculously oversized tie. Not just any ridiculously oversized tie, however. People who preorder First Light for Switch 2 get the GoldenEye Suit, and it includes the suit and tie that Pierce Brosnan wore in the famous 1995 movie, including the oversized tie. Brosnan wore a lot of suits in that movie, but the one being referenced here is the one with the oversized tie, which was the style at the time. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ONqZeuZtbVE GoldenEye has a special history with Nintendo specifically, which may help explain why Switch 2 owners are getting this outfit and no one else is. After all, 1997's GoldenEye 007, which was based on the movie, is one of the most iconic N64 games of all time. First Light has been a big hit, critically and commercially, scoring great reviews and selling more than 4 million copies , and that's before the Switch 2 version even comes out. The Switch 2 version of First Light was supposed to launch alongside the other versions in May 2026, but was later delayed multiple times. IO said a combination of factors contributed to delays. In addition to the forthcoming Switch 2 version of First Light, IO is working on a new fantasy game. However, after Xbox pulled funding, IO laid off staff. Many also want to see IO work on the expected sequel to First Light , but no official announcements have been made.

gamespot.com/articles/were-getting-a-wwe.title: We’re Getting A WWE And Street Fighter Crossover, And It’s Pretty Weird
gamespot.com/articles/were-getting-a-wwe.excerpt: Ahead of the Street Fighter movie 's release this week, 2K Games has announced a new DLC pack for WWE 2K26 that lets you dress several WWE performers as Street Fighter action figures . Pricing hasn't been revealed yet, but generally, these character packs cost around $15. Bison Rey Mysterio as Ryu Bianca Belair as Cammy Ultimate Warrior as Blanka Dominik Mysterio as Ken Strangely, there's no Cody Rhodes Street Fighter skin, which is kind of weird since he plays Guile in the movie and has even cosplayed as him at WWE live events.  Additionally, the pack includes 15 Create-a-Superstar parts from several other Street Fighter characters: Akuma, Vega, and Chun-Li. Reviews have also begun appearing online for Street Fighter, and on GameSpot's sister site Metacritic , the film has a "mixed or average" metascore of 46 from 19 reviews. Critics say that the movie's story is an absolute mess, and it's barely held together by several stylish fight scenes across its two-hour runtime. The movie isn't tracking well for its opening weekend either , as current estimates suggest that it could struggle to make a dent at the box office. At least popcorn bucket sales should be a hit.

gamespot.com/articles/the-blood-of-dawnw.excerpt: The Blood of Dawnwalker is already one of the best role-playing games of the year, but developer Rebel Wolves is preparing a big update that should make it even better. Like all good things in life, it starts with getting to pet a dog. Update 1.1, which is scheduled to arrive next week, brings a number of new features to the game, including the ability to pet both dogs and cats via the game's directional system, which is currently only used for combat. It will also feature a new Story difficulty setting that provides "additional combat assist," new subtitle settings across all lines of dialogue, and most crucially, an item called Draught of Mind Rebirth. The Draught of Mind Rebirth will allow you to forget all the skills and abilities you've acquired across the Swordmastery, Witchcraft, and Vampirism trees. Not only will this give you the chance to reallocate your points in a way that best fits your playstyle--it will also give you back the time associated with those skills. That means you'll have the chance to complete extra missions if you happen to find yourself impeded with Dawnwalker's 30-day limit. However, we don't find the system to be restrictive as it currently stands. The Blood of Dawnwalker Update 1.1 Alongside the new features, Update 1.1. will also feature some tweaks to existing systems. These include an update to the FrameGen system, improvements to the camera, better Shadowstep and Planeshift abilities, and the removal of censorship of blood in the Japanese version. It will also include combat improvements that should make it easier to correctly target your enemy of choice--currently, it's a little finicky because of the direction-based system which prioritizes you blocking incoming attacks--regardless of who's trying to strike you--over you focusing in on a particular enemy. It turns out that recent AI updates--like the release of Claude Opus 5.5--are making it very easy to reverse-engineer the source code for a game and get it running in a browser. What are vibe-coded browser ports? You've probably heard of vibe-coding by now, as this generally involves a person tasking an AI agent with generating, refactoring, and gluing code back together. I'm simplifying things here, but essentially, you tell the AI what you want, and it'll then write the code for you, as well as provide fixes. A vibe-coded browser port is essentially a video game that has been decompiled and then made playable on a website using AI; instead of downloading a massive file or installing an emulator to play the game, you just click a link, and you can start playing a game in your browser. So far, people have used AI to create all kinds of browser ports, ranging from classic console games to mash-ups of recent titles. Instead, Alliance Arts will hold closed online play sessions for a limited number of players. https://youtu.be/SRFDW2Pm9nk "We sincerely apologize for the short notice to everyone who was looking forward to it," the developer wrote online . "We're concerned that the demo's content could be used to quickly imitate or replicate the game's presentation and gameplay with AI or other tools, and that such works could be released before our launch." Alliance Arts is also concerned that it can't properly manage restrictions on posting and streaming content from the game, and it'll instead hand out demo keys and collect feedback for the game through its group Discord. The studio's fears aren't unwarranted, with the upcoming Needle in a Haystack being a prime example of Steam's copycat problem. After the game was announced in August and a clip of its purposefully tedious gameplay went viral--you genuinely are just looking for a needle in a haystack--clones quickly popped up online. A quick search on Steam reveals several games all with a similar theme, and these have been released within weeks of each other. Looks a little sus to me. What happened here? AI-assisted games have been popping up more and more lately on Steam, and while you'll seldom find disclosure text indicating that agents like Claude and ChatGPT have been used in their development, the fast turnaround, near-identical gameplay, and artwork with a telltale yellow filter suggest that the tech played a heavy hand in quickly whipping up a clone. That pressure on Microsoft has had results, as last year, the company did block the Israeli government from accessing its cloud storage and AI systems, which has reportedly been used to surveil Palestinians in both the West Bank and Gaza. gamespot.com/articles/killing-ps5-discs-.title: Killing PS5 Discs Just Makes Sense, Even If It Angers People, Former PlayStation Exec Says
gamespot.com/articles/killing-ps5-discs-.excerpt: Ken Kutaragi, the former PlayStation executive known colloquially as the "Father of PlayStation," has reacted to the ongoing debate and discussion about physical games in the wake of Sony's announcement that it will end support for PS5 game discs in 2028. Speaking to VGC , Kutaragi said he understands that people think they "own" games when they buy them physically. However, he said, "Nobody thinks [physical media] is necessary for a networked device like a smartphone, for example, because people feel that they will keep their content." He went on to say that he "really" does understand why some people are upset about PlayStation's decision to end discs. After all, Sony continues to sell millions and millions of physical games annually , and in some regions, sales of new games on PS5 are more than 50% physical . However, as many others have said and data shows, consumers are increasingly leaning toward digital, and that trend is only expected to continue. "I don’t think it’s economically reasonable [to continue to support discs]. Maybe it’s a mentality issue," he said. For its part, Sony said ending support for physical discs is a "natural direction" for the company as it adapts to consumer trends. As such, he thinks it only makes sense that these new hires might see PlayStation as "not just a game console, but also a content terminal." "Maybe that’s how those people are thinking. gamespot.com/articles/over-the-hill-is-a.title: Over The Hill Is Already At Its Lowest Price, So Join Me By Taking The Scenic Route
gamespot.com/articles/over-the-hill-is-a.excerpt: Driving in a crowded town, with frequent stopping and starting as you wait for the hustle and bustle of daily life to fade, is, quite frankly, dull. I don’t mind blaring my music and singing out of tune to Zac Efron’s "Bet On It" as much as the next guy, but the reality is simple: Normal driving is boring. However, take away the road and head for the wilderness, and things get more interesting. That’s exactly what Over the Hill asks you to do. While most of the “friendslop” games around right now (which I think is just a silly subgenre name for some of the best co-op games , but I digress) focus on horror experiences or absurd worlds, Over the Hill is fittingly distinct in its normality. You and your friends drive cars through a stylized wilderness, heading off the tarmac and into scenic landscapes while helping each other overcome the obstacles in your way. Thunderstorms roll across the sky, bringing treacherous weather to your journey, before the storm clouds lift to reveal blue skies and a gentle sunset. Thick mud makes it difficult to get your car moving, but a handy winch lets your friends pull you out of the sludge and back on your way. Along the journey, you can also look for potential upgrades to make things a little easier before the next obstacle appears. Even if you’re a fan of racing games and feel truly comfortable behind the wheel, Over the Hill offers a different way to experience driving. This isn’t about reaching your destination faster; it’s about the journey. And when that journey takes you past beautiful lakes at sunrise or through snow-covered mountains that become more accessible as you plow through the terrain, well, it’s a journey worth taking. The game has only just launched, but if you’re looking to pick it up at a discount, you can grab it for just $15.74 / £14.17 at Fanatical . French developer Sunny Lab and publisher Silver Lining Interactive don’t think so, if The Witch’s Bakery is anything to go by. This narrative-led adventure sim is filled with cute characters, emotional stories, and pastries. And although you can’t smell the baked goods themselves, you can immerse yourself in Parisian – and otherworldly – wonderlands. You get flavours of Kiki’s Delivery Service throughout the game: anime art style, young witch protagonist, sassy familiar, bakery setting, not to mention emotional storyline. But instead of delivering for the bakery, this witch works in the bakery. And instead of flying, her main power is seeing into people’s hearts. Sunny Lab mixes these ingredients together to serve up a game that’s hearty and moreish, even if it doesn’t all go down smoothly. Read the full article on nintendolife.com

During the time that the stress test is live, the game's closed beta will be offline, but will return following the conclusion of the test. All characters made during the stress test will be deleted once the test is over. It's not much, but for those who wanted to at least dabble in WoW: Forever without having to buy the $60 Skyborne Epic Pack for a beta code, the stress test will at least let curious players dip their toes in. Even the beta itself won't be around for much longer. It will run until October 21, after which it will shut down and characters will be deleted to make way for early name reservations for the full game on October 27. gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-just-c.title: WoW: Forever Just Changed The Math On What Race To Play In A Big Way
gamespot.com/articles/wow-forever-just-c.excerpt: World of Warcraft: Forever's beta is set to end in just a few days on October 21, but that hasn't stopped Blizzard from making some major changes to the game's various racial abilities. Unlike in the modern version of WoW, where racial abilities are so minor that they mostly feel cosmetic, racial abilities in WoW Classic (and now in Forever) are a big part of why players choose to play a particular race. Some races synergise better with certain classes or playstyles. Others even benefit more from using specific types of weapons. Or at least they used to. In Forever's latest beta update, developer Blizzard has overhauled many of the MMO's racial abilities to remove weapon-specific buffs and improve some abilities that were seen as lackluster by the community. The removal of weapon-based passives for humans, dwarves, and orcs is a significant change. Orcs used to favor axes, humans swords and maces, and dwarves guns. In WoW Classic, that meant an increased weapon skill when using those weapons, resulting in a better chance to hit and increased damage. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=miSndSl23bI That changed for WoW: Forever's beta. Blizzard kept some of the weapon-specific flavor, but instead of weapon skill, pivoted to critical-strike chance. Now with this latest update, those bonuses no longer require players of a certain race to wield a specific weapon type to gain those passive benefits. Orcs simply gain a 1% increase to crit chance, humans gain a 2% increase to crit chance, and dwarves deal 2% increased critical damage and healing at all times. It's a major departure, but feels like it will ultimately allow for more freedom when it comes to using a variety of weapons. Those weren't the only racial ability changes though. gamespot.com/articles/how-long-is-call-o.excerpt: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's campaign is live in early access, with the full game arriving on October 23. Modern Warfare 4's single-player experience brings the epic story conclusion to Infinity Ward's rebooted Modern Warfare series. The Modern Warfare 4 campaign is slightly longer than recent Call of Duty games, and there are rewards you can unlock as you play. This guide will break down exactly what to expect for missions and rewards. How long to beat the Modern Warfare 4 campaign? It'll take you around eight hours to complete Modern Warfare 4's campaign on normal difficulty. In recent years, Call of Duty campaigns have averaged around 5-6 hours to complete, but Modern Warfare 4's story is lengthier. However, you might need more time if you choose a higher difficulty or plan on achievement hunting. Modern Warfare 4 also has one open-world mission called "Stranded" that offers optional exploration. Modern Warfare 4 includes 16 missions in total, and each mission unlocks a campaign reward. These rewards are a mix of cosmetic items and double XP tokens for use in MW4. gamespot.com/reviews/call-of-duty-modern.title: CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Goes Back To Basics To Properly Finish Its Story
gamespot.com/reviews/call-of-duty-modern.excerpt: In 2019, Infinity Ward rebooted Call of Duty's Modern Warfare series, delivering a gritty and polished campaign featuring Captain Price and the assembly of the iconic Task Force 141. Despite the strong start, the series' sequels stumbled a bit, with  Modern Warfare 3 in particular standing out as having a weak story and open-world missions that missed the mark. But with Modern Warfare 4, Infinity Ward returns the series' campaign to strength with a satisfying narrative and well-crafted missions for an epic conclusion to the rebooted series. Modern Warfare 4's single-player goes back to being a traditional and mostly linear experience that some recent entries have strayed from. There is only one open-world mission this year, and it is far more engaging than the previous attempts. Modern Warfare 4 doesn't introduce anything new or innovative, but it finds success with a consistently strong narrative and engaging gameplay built on nail-biting tension. Thankfully, you're never forced into any mission objectives that feel like silly chores or ill-timed distractions. Every mission in Modern Warfare 4 carries urgency and drives the plot forward. That plot closes out the ongoing narrative surrounding Price and Task Force 141, but it also takes Call of Duty to Korea and introduces a fresh new cast of characters. The campaign intertwines two seemingly separate stories for an over-the-top, globetrotting affair across New York City, Paris, and Mumbai, in addition to several parts of Korea. This is the explosive Hollywood-style action you'd expect from a Call of Duty campaign at a quality level we haven't seen from the franchise in years--that includes the recent Black Ops entries. One half of the game places you in the boots of Private Park, a young South Korean soldier, who has never experienced real combat before. Especially during this spookily festive time of year, I sometimes find atmospheric tension more enjoyable than jump scares. Silver Pines delivers that fear in droves. Don’t believe me? Well, give it a try now that it’s cheaper than ever. Taking beloved horror experiences and twisting them into one of the most memorable metroidvania games in recent memory isn’t a simple task. It requires taking elements from beloved genres and contorting them into something unique. Silver Pines does just that, with a dash of Twin Peaks thrown in for good measure. You play as private investigator Red Walker as he searches for Eddie Velvet, a missing musician who has seemingly vanished. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=INvwzryTXAw&pp=ygUUc2lsdmVyIHBpbmVzIHRyYWlsZXI%3D Like many small American towns (in media, of course), Silver Pines is home to plenty of mysteries and a dark atmosphere that you can only truly appreciate by playing the game. Or, well, watching the trailer and realizing that there’s definitely something wrong. The visual design really emphasizes that feeling, and the game feels smooth as butter as you wander deserted roads and explore empty buildings. Of course, it’s not all about investigating. Eventually, you’ll have to fight creatures that look like they were pulled directly out of Konami’s horror franchise, but Walker isn’t some mercenary who’s skilled with every firearm. Combat is challenging, and with limited inventory space, every shot matters. Reloading your revolver, for example, requires well-timed button presses to load bullets into the chamber, making every fight more intense. gamespot.com/articles/no-publisher-wante.title: No Publisher Wanted Outlast. 60 Million Players Later, The Horror Juggernaut Is Doing Just Fine.
gamespot.com/articles/no-publisher-wante.excerpt: Let's play Family Feud. Poll 100 people on the scariest game they've ever played. What's on the board? Surely a Silent Hill, and a Resident Evil, too. Alien Isolation seems likely. One of the Fatal Frames has a good shot. Those who know ball may call out a deeper cut like Siren, Sylvio, or Visage. One name I'm certain makes it on the board--to the tune of my family cheering me on with "Good answer! Good answer!"--is Outlast . The horror game from Montreal-based indie studio Red Barrels was released in 2013 as the debut effort from what was then a 10-person team. The studio was founded by developers with an origin story we hear about a lot in the games industry: They left roles at big-budget studios like Electronic Arts, Ubisoft, and Naughty Dog to pursue something they could call their own. On an hour-long call with Red Barrels' Phillipe Morin, he told me how he and his co-founders, David Chateauneuf and Hugo Dallaire, established Red Barrels as a fully independent game studio and built what has become a tentpole horror series. Content warning: This article contains descriptions of extreme violence. "After our project got canceled at EA, we were having a hard time picking up on where we would want to go, what we would want to do," Morin said. "And so I think that's when we realized that we were pretty much all at the same place career-wise [and felt] it was time we try to make a project of our own." Morin said the burgeoning team didn't know what its first game would be, but they landed on a horror game because that's what they were passionate about, with a distinct style to stand out: first-person, defenseless in nature--players could only run and hide from enemies, not fight back--with what would become the game's signature night-vision lens coloring the terror lurking around every corner. gamespot.com/articles/fire-emblems-remar.title: Fire Emblem’s Remarkable Comeback
gamespot.com/articles/fire-emblems-remar.excerpt: Though it may not be a sales juggernaut on the scale of Mario or The Legend of Zelda, Fire Emblem is one of Nintendo's preeminent franchises. Like so many of its vaunted stablemates, the series is almost as old as Nintendo's gaming ambitions, debuting on the Famicom and appearing on nearly every home and handheld console since. Given this prominence, it's almost difficult to believe that Fire Emblem's future was ever in jeopardy, but such was indeed once the case; there was a point in time when the series was very much on the verge of cancellation, and it took a dramatic shakeup to reverse its fortunes. To fully contextualize this rocky period in Fire Emblem's history, we need to look back at its trajectory in the wake of its belated international debut. Unlike Nintendo's other marquee properties, Fire Emblem took a circuitous route to Western markets. Though the series began in 1990, its first several installments were never released outside of Japan, and most Western players would end up being introduced to the franchise not through one of its mainline entries, but through Super Smash Bros. Melee for the Nintendo GameCube. Even more so than its predecessor, Melee was a veritable celebration of Nintendo history. The game drew deeply from the company's rich oeuvre; its roster was stuffed with beloved mascots, and its extensive array of collectible trophies covered the full sweep of the publisher's gaming legacy, from renowned classics to obscure curios. What generated the most chatter among international players, however, were two particular hidden fighters who hailed from a series most had never heard of: Marth, hero of the first Fire Emblem , and Roy, protagonist of the series' then-newest installment, The Binding Blade. Despite their unfamiliarity, these mysterious swordsmen instantly became two of Melee's most popular characters thanks to their cool designs and nimble swordplay, which helped set them apart from the more recognizable characters on the roster. gamespot.com/articles/tenebris-somnia-bl.title: Tenebris Somnia Blends 2D Visuals With Live-Action Horror Scenes, And It’s Already On Sale At Launch
gamespot.com/articles/tenebris-somnia-bl.excerpt: Horror games live or die by their scares and tension. If the player isn’t uncomfortable guiding a character through dreadful situations, well, you may as well be playing an action-adventure game (don’t mention the first Uncharted’s final act, please). Tenebris Somnia blends the discomfort of retro horror with live-action sequences that will make your goosebumps bump, and you can get it cheaper than ever right now. As the best horror games continue to push for more realistic visuals and immersive experiences, Tenebris Somnia’s twist on the genre combines old-school cool with movie-like cutscenes. It’s both jarring and original, and that’s exactly what makes for excellent horror. I want to be constantly surprised, and Tenebris Somnia makes its pixelated 2D threats even more menacing when you see live-action versions of the monsters. Inspired by classics that scared us silly, like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, Tenebris Somnia has a deceptively simple premise. You play as Julia, who finds herself in a parallel universe while visiting her ex-boyfriend and is relentlessly hunted by nightmares that, well, aren’t exactly figments of her imagination. (To be honest, visiting an ex sounds like a nightmarish experience on its own.
